title: Valid Parentheses
interviewTips: Ask if input contains only '()[]{}' and what to return for empty string (LeetCode: true).
Trade-off: repeated string replacement is simple but O(n^2); stack with hash map is O(n) and is the expected optimal.
Edge cases: empty string, single bracket, wrong order like '([)]', and unclosed opens like '(((' - always check stack empty before pop.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Repeated Pair Elimination
approaches.intuition: A valid string can be fully reduced by repeatedly deleting adjacent matching pairs '()', '[]', '{}'. If after no more deletions anything remains, it is invalid.
approaches.theory: This simulates reduction to empty. Each pass scans the string and removes innermost pairs. Correct because any valid sequence must contain at least one adjacent matching pair unless empty, and removing it preserves validity of the remainder. Repeating until fixpoint decides validity.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each pass scans O(n) to replace, and up to O(n/2) passes in worst case like '((((...))))', plus string copy/erase cost O(n) per deletion.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Each replace/erase creates a new string of size up to n.

steps: pass1: no substring '()','[]','{}' found, s unchanged='([)]'

edgeCases: Empty string '' => true (no brackets to mismatch)
Single char '(' => false (no pair to remove)
Nested valid '([]{})' => reduces to empty => true

approaches.name: Approach 2: Stack with Closing-to-Opening Map
approaches.intuition: Scan left to right: push opens, on close check top of stack matches. LIFO order enforces correct nesting.
approaches.theory: Brackets form a well-parenthesized language requiring last-opened-first-closed. A stack exactly models this. Use hash map close->open for O(1) match. If close with empty stack or mismatch => invalid. At end stack must be empty (all opens closed). Single pass is sufficient and necessary.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single left-to-right scan, each char pushed/popped at most once, hash map lookup O(1).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Stack holds at most n opening brackets in worst case like '((((...', plus O(1) map.

steps: s='()[]{}': push '(' then see ')' matches pop => stack=[]
push '[' then see ']' matches pop => stack=[]
push '{' then see '}' matches pop => stack=[] => true
s='([)]': push '(' push '[' then see ')' top is '[' mismatch => false

edgeCases: '(' or ')' alone => false (empty pop or leftover)
'(]' and '([)]' => false (order matters, stack catches mismatch)
Long opens '((((...))))' => true, stack depth n/2
